newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Steady along with firm crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Steady along with firm crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady at midday on Tuesday in quiet trading amid jitters that the mild resurgence in demand would not be enough to absorb the abundant regional supplies, traders said.
The firmer crude values were providing stability to gas oil prices, they said.

July swaps were indicated at $22.50/$22.65 per barrel, almost unchanged from Monday. August was quoted at $22.95/$23.10, up five to 10 cents from Monday in a steep contango market with September quoted at $23.45/$23.60.
August Brent crude futures closed 36 cents higher in London on Monday at $18.51 per barrel, while July gas oil futures settled at $165.25 per tonne, up $1.50.
They said gas oil cargoes from Northeast Asia would put added pressure on supplies.
Japanese refiners were expected to export more amid deregulation from July while South Korean refiners were also selling physical cargoes at discount levels.
Traders noted that buyers stayed away as cheap offers vanished with the lowest physical offer seen on Monday at $165 per tonne ($22.15 per barrel) with three offers at $22.40.
Traders noted that buyers such as China and Indonesia had emerged earlier to take advantage of cheap oil but would be more cautious now that sellers were offering at firmer prices.
Jet fuel prices were steady with the swaps regrade almost unchanged for July at $2.00/$2.20, and August and September at $1.70/$1/95.

Buyers for the forward months were bidding at 10 cents below Monday amid concerns that increased jet fuel production and the opening of the arbitrage from the West might raise supplies beyond the region's capacity to absorb them.
Fuel oil also remained steady despite selling pressure on the physical market on Monday, held up mainly by the firmer crude, brokers said.
July swaps was quoted at $98.50/$99.00 per tonne, and August at $98.00/$98.50.
